items.item: The same three garment designs retain their colours, relaxed proportions, neckline, opening, hem, pocket, bands and repair details across all flat-lays and wearing views.
Removing and carrying C01 changes only its wearing state; the exposed P01 and carried C01 remain the garments established in the journey layering view.
The collection forms one coordinated autumn-and-winter wardrobe while allowing the designer to choose unspecified neckline, hem and pocket details.
Patch and cuff states preserve the P01 components, attachment locations, material structures and dimensions established by the specifications and back flat-lay.
The palette and knit studies agree on style colours, M01 body/sleeve/patch applications and M02 cuff/band applications, with a washed, unbrushed surface character.

Repair demonstrations show removable components and reusable sleeve interfaces; size changes preserve the fixed patch geometry and 60 mm cuff depth while using the specified S, M and L joining circumferences.

requirementChecks.criteria: Read the original file properties: Format: presentation document; at least eight actual pages. Stage: final.

Where knit surfaces are resolved, M01 has a double moss structure and M02 has paired knit-and-purl rib columns at a compatible fine-gauge scale. Bodies, sleeves and patches use M01; cuffs and neckline, hem and cardigan opening bands use M02. Surfaces have a washed, unbrushed character. View distance and lighting may reduce detail, but a clearly different stitch structure or brushed pile fails. Any printed material records must agree with the fixed composition, gauge, weights and usable widths; those physical properties need not be inferred from a photograph.

Each of the three label enlargements is associated with its own garment and represents an inside centre-back-neck label, with the collection name above the repair message. The label represents a 75 × 20 mm component; enlargement for readability is allowed. Reversed line order, a missing garment label, an exterior label location or contradictory dimensions fails.

P01 and C01 cuff interfaces, wherever exposed or explained, support removal by undoing hand linking around the sleeve opening. An enlarged interface must allow access to linking-yarn ends inside the sleeve seam. Ordinary wearing views may conceal those ends. Integral knitting, a cut-off sleeve, a zipper or another incompatible replacement mechanism fails.
Resolved attachment stitches on either patch colour are Navy. Lighting and small-scale loss of stitch detail are allowed; clearly contrasting stitch yarn in another colour fails.

The three documents establish the collection and style/material identities with consistent meanings. The craft sheet records both materials as 80% wool/20% nylon, 12 gauge and washed/unbrushed; M01 as double moss, 380 g/m², 1400 mm usable width and 8 × 8 mm repeat; M02 as 2 × 2 rib, 420 g/m² and 1000 mm width. It assigns M01 to bodies, sleeves and patches and M02 to cuffs and bands, specifies matching-yarn linked seams, removable full-circumference cuff hand linking with accessible yarn ends, patch construction and Navy running stitches, the 75 × 20 mm two-line inside-back-neck label and five 18 mm corozo buttons. The size note contains the size records and grading. The plan maps Rust #9B513D to P01, Navy #253544 to C01 and Cream #E6DDCA to V01, their shared materials and six specified wearing combinations. Information may use prose, tables or diagrams within its assigned document; omissions or contradictions fail.

The note contains all nine style-size records in mm. P01 S/M/L chest values are 1040/1120/1200, body lengths 620/640/660 and underarm sleeve lengths 460/480/500. C01 values are chest 1200/1280/1360, body 700/720/740 and sleeve 440/460/480. V01 chest values are 1120/1200/1280 and body lengths 650/670/690, with sleeve and cuff fields inapplicable. P01/C01 cuff circumferences are 220/240/260 and depths are 60 throughout. Both grade steps explicitly add 80 mm chest and 20 mm body length for every style, plus 20 mm sleeve length and cuff circumference for P01/C01. The note preserves 80 × 100 mm patches and a 180 mm centre offset in every size, and distinguishes relaxed full circumferences, high-shoulder-point body length and sleeve length excluding cuff depth. Missing rows, increments or incorrect measurement definitions fail.

The presentation legibly reproduces all nine S/M/L style records, including chest circumference, body length, applicable underarm sleeve length, cuff joining circumference and cuff depth. Values match the fixed client table and the size note; V01 sleeve and cuff fields remain inapplicable. Tables may be rearranged across pages. A size-M-only summary, missing fields or faithfully repeating an erroneous source value fails.

Every flat-lay gives the size-M records for each style it depicts: P01 chest/body/sleeve 1120/640/480 mm, C01 1280/720/460 mm and V01 chest/body 1200/670 mm. P01 and C01 also show 240 mm cuff joining circumference and 60 mm cuff depth. Collection views cover all three styles; enlarged views cover their own style. Clearly associated keys are acceptable; missing measurements, incorrect values or sleeve lengths that include the separate cuff depth fail.

Each image prints its applicable style and material IDs consistently with the specifications. Collection views and the palette identify P01, C01, V01, M01 and M02; individual garment views identify their own style and both materials; patch details identify P01/M01; cuff details distinguish the P01 M01 sleeve and M02 cuff; studies identify their material and stated style applications. Callouts or a key are acceptable. Missing relevant IDs or incorrect material-to-component assignments fail.

The presentation includes COMMON LOOP, all three style IDs and both material IDs with their established meanings. It repeats all six plan combinations: seated P01 at home; P01/V01/open C01 at the office; P01 under closed C01 walking; C01 over a plain base at home; the journey outfit with C01 removed and carried to expose P01; and V01 over a plain base at the office. A readable combination table or equivalent captions are acceptable; missing combinations, changed garment states or inconsistent identities fail.

Every depicted style and component retains its assigned body-and-rib colour: Rust P01, Navy C01 and Cream V01, with Cream P01 patches and Rust C01 patches. The palette links the supplied colour codes to the three styles and M01/M02. Collection-front and cardigan-front each show exactly five corozo cardigan buttons and communicate their 18 mm size. All three collection-front label enlargements make both required lines readable. Lighting may shift apparent colour; reassigned colours, an incorrect button count or illegible labels fails.

The presentation includes a label page with readable COMMON LOOP above Made to be mended and preserves the specified style-colour assignments in its written records. A legible reused label illustration is acceptable; a missing page, altered text, reversed lines or contradictory colour assignment fails.

The material studies establish a dimensioned 8 × 8 mm M01 double moss repeat and recognizable 2 × 2 M02 rib. Resolved garment and repair surfaces retain those structures and compatible scale. Collection-back, pullover-back, cardigan-back and both patch details each dimension the applicable patches as 80 mm across by 100 mm along the sleeve, with their centres on the rear sleeve line 180 mm above the cuff joining seam. Each P01/C01 sleeve has its own external patch. Perspective and knit deformation are allowed; changed structures, missing required dimensions or incorrect patch orientation or placement fails.

Readable presentation annotations specify 80 × 100 mm patches and a patch-centre position 180 mm above the cuff joining seam, consistent with the size note and repair images. A reused dimensioned detail is sufficient. Missing dimensions, switched orientation or an offset measured to a patch edge fails.

The patch pair preserves the same Rust P01 elbow and Cream patch; the cuff pair preserves the same Rust P01 sleeve and matching Rust M02 cuff. Removed components lie beside their intact exposed attachment areas. The attached patch labels vertical running stitches at 5 mm stitch length, 5 mm gaps, 10 mm row spacing and 5 mm edge inset. Both cuff details label 240 mm joining circumference and 60 mm depth and show a compatible removable hand-linked interface. The rib study identifies 2 × 2 rib and labels S/M/L interfaces as 220/240/260 mm with 60 mm cuff depth. Changed components, destructive removal, missing loose pieces or incorrect dimensions fail.

The presentation explicitly associates relaxed cuff joining circumferences of 220, 240 and 260 mm with S, M and L respectively, agreeing with the size note and rib study. A readable table or reused annotated study is acceptable; missing sizes, swapped values or treating these figures as flat widths fails.

The images cover all six assigned states: seated P01 at home; office P01 under V01 under open C01; walking P01 under closed C01; home C01 over a plain base; the journey outfit with the same C01 removed and carried, exposing matching P01 details; and office V01 over a plain base. The office layering view shows three distinct neckline or opening shapes plus at least one Cream P01 patch and one Rust C01 patch. Home P01 and C01 views expose their respective repair and knit details; the vest-only view makes neckline, armholes and hem readable. Different poses are allowed; missing situations, substituted garment details or concealed required office features fail.

Review the entire 12-second video for standing, reaching for a desk item and walking in the office combination. Rust P01 remains beneath Cream V01 beneath open Navy C01, with separately discernible neckline/opening shapes and consistent garment and repair geometry. Resolved surfaces preserve the M01 repeat and M02 rib. The closing frame legibly names COMMON LOOP, P01, C01 and V01. Camera and pose changes are allowed; missing actions, incompatible garments or textures, incorrect duration or incomplete closing names fails.

requirementChecks.criteria: The presentation has at least ten pages and visibly incorporates material from all three specification documents and each of the nineteen delivered images, plus three identifiable stills from the movement video. Reused views preserve garment identities, colours and repair construction. Scaling, cropping and layout changes are acceptable when source identity and required information remain legible. A source mentioned only by name, an omitted source, substituted imagery or fewer than three video stills fails.

The same three garment designs retain their colours, relaxed proportions, neckline, opening, hem, pocket, bands and repair details across all flat-lays and wearing views. Removing and carrying C01 changes only its wearing state; the exposed P01 and carried C01 remain the garments established in the journey layering view. The collection forms one coordinated autumn-and-winter wardrobe while allowing the designer to choose unspecified neckline, hem and pocket details.

Patch and cuff states preserve the P01 components, attachment locations, material structures and dimensions established by the specifications and back flat-lay. The palette and knit studies agree on style colours, M01 body/sleeve/patch applications and M02 cuff/band applications, with a washed, unbrushed surface character. Repair demonstrations show removable components and reusable sleeve interfaces; size changes preserve the fixed patch geometry and 60 mm cuff depth while using the specified S, M and L joining circumferences.
